definition: A system in which a language model repeatedly reasons about a goal, chooses an action (such as a tool call or search), and observes the result.
details: Agents pair a model with a loop of perception, reasoning and action so it can complete multi-step tasks rather than producing a single answer. ReAct interleaves “reasoning traces” with actions and observations, which improves factuality and lets models answer and act in one framework. Agent frameworks commonly add memory, planning and a set of tools the model can invoke.
story: Picture hiring a brilliant new assistant on their first morning — smart, motivated, but with no idea how anything in your office actually works. It plans a little, acts a little, looks at the result, and then decides what to do next. It is the difference between a search engine and a helper who actually finishes the task. It is a loop of look, act, and learn — the same way you cook from a recipe you have never tried: add, taste, correct. And that habit of checking, acting, then checking again is AI Agent.

citation.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
